input.requirements_spec: See C1-03 gold standard: enable accepted creators to submit content drafts for campaign collaborations. Submissions pass through an automated validation pipeline (text length, image count, sensitive word detection, image quality API) before reaching the brand. Supports iterative revision workflow with version history. States: draft → auto_checking → auto_rejected/pending_review → revision_requested → approved → published. Max revisions configurable per campaign. Deadline enforcement via UTC comparison.
input.system_context: Existing FastAPI microservice (campaign-service) with Python 3.11, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery. Existing modules: User (model/repo/service/API with CRUD, soft-delete, pagination), Campaign (assumed created by C2-01), Application (assumed created by C2-02). Layered architecture: Model → Repository → Service → API. Uses SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic v2 schemas, custom AppError exceptions. Auth via X-User-Id header with role-based access. See existing user_repo.py, user_service.py, users.py for patterns.
input.constraints: Submission API must respond within 500ms (p95). Auto-check pipeline must complete within 30 seconds. External image quality API has 10-second timeout. Version numbers must be strictly sequential with no gaps. Media files are pre-uploaded to XHS CDN — submissions contain CDN URLs only.

module_design.overview: Two new SQLAlchemy models (ContentSubmission, ContentVersion), corresponding Pydantic schemas, a SubmissionRepository for data access, a SubmissionService for business logic, an API router mounted at /api/v1, and a ContentValidator utility that orchestrates the auto-check pipeline.

new_files.purpose: ContentSubmission and ContentVersion SQLAlchemy models with SubmissionStatus enum
Pydantic schemas: SubmissionCreate, SubmissionResponse, VersionResponse, ValidationResultResponse
SubmissionRepository class following the UserRepository pattern
SubmissionService class with submit, resubmit, list_versions, get_submission logic
ContentValidator class orchestrating the auto-check pipeline (text, image count, sensitive words, image quality)
FastAPI router for submission endpoints, mounted at /api/v1

modified_files.change: Add ContentSubmission and ContentVersion to __all__ exports
Include submissions router with prefix /submissions and /applications/{id}/submissions

tables.name: content_submissions
tables.description: Tracks the overall submission lifecycle for an application. One row per application.

tables.name: content_versions
tables.description: Stores each immutable version of submitted content. One row per submission attempt.

relationships: ContentSubmission has MANY-TO-ONE Application (application_id FK, unique — one submission per application)

integration_points.purpose: Verify the creator has an accepted application for the campaign. Fetch campaign requirements (min_word_count, min_image_count, max_image_count, content_deadline, max_revisions).
integration_points.interface: Direct repository query (same database) — ApplicationRepository.get_by_id(application_id) with status=accepted check
integration_points.failure_handling: If application not found or not accepted, raise NotFoundError or ForbiddenError

integration_points.purpose: Fetch campaign requirements for auto-check validation and deadline enforcement
integration_points.interface: Direct repository query — CampaignRepository.get_by_id(campaign_id) to read content requirements and deadlines
integration_points.failure_handling: If campaign not found, raise NotFoundError

integration_points.purpose: Check submitted text body against a list of restricted terms
integration_points.interface: SensitiveWordChecker.check(text: str) -> list[str] — returns list of detected sensitive words. Loaded from config/sensitive_words.txt at startup.
integration_points.failure_handling: If word list file missing, log error and skip check (treat as passed with warning)

integration_points.purpose: Score image quality (resolution, clarity, composition) for each submitted image URL
integration_points.interface: HTTP POST to configured IMAGE_QUALITY_API_URL with {"image_url": "..."} → {"score": float 0-100, "details": {...}}. Threshold: score >= 60 to pass.
integration_points.failure_handling: 10-second timeout per image. On timeout or error: mark check as 'skipped' with reason 'Image quality service unavailable'. Submission proceeds to pending_review with incomplete_checks flag. Retry via Celery with exponential backoff (1s, 4s, 16s), max 3 retries.

integration_points.purpose: Notify brand when submission passes auto-check and enters pending_review. Notify creator when auto-check fails or when submission expires.
integration_points.failure_handling: Fire-and-forget. Notification failure does not block submission flow. Failed notifications are logged and retried by the notification service.

technical_decisions.decision: Auto-check pipeline runs synchronously within the API request for v1
alternatives_considered: Async via Celery task — returns immediately with status=auto_checking, creator polls for result
Synchronous chain within the API handler — runs checks sequentially, returns final status
technical_decisions.rationale: For v1, the pipeline has only 4 checks and the longest (image quality API) has a 10-second timeout. Total worst-case is ~15 seconds, well within the 30-second pipeline SLA. Synchronous avoids the complexity of polling/websocket for status updates. If the external API is consistently slow, migrate to async in v2.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: Blocks the creator's request for up to ~15 seconds. Acceptable for v1 UX since submission is an infrequent, high-intent action.

technical_decisions.decision: Store each content version as a separate row in content_versions table
alternatives_considered: JSON array of versions in a single content_submissions column
Separate table with one row per version
technical_decisions.rationale: Separate rows enable efficient queries (e.g., 'get version 2 of submission X' without parsing JSON), enforce unique constraint on (submission_id, version_number), allow individual version indexing, and support pagination over version history. JSON array would require full-document reads and writes, and cannot enforce uniqueness at the DB level.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: Slightly more complex joins when fetching a submission with its latest version. Mitigated by the current_version field on content_submissions that points to the latest version number.

technical_decisions.decision: Media files are referenced by CDN URL, not stored by campaign-service
alternatives_considered: Accept file uploads in the submission API and store in object storage
Accept CDN URLs only, validate domain whitelist
technical_decisions.chosen: CDN URLs only, with domain whitelist validation
technical_decisions.rationale: Media upload is already handled by XHS's existing Content service. Duplicating upload logic in campaign-service would be redundant and increase storage costs. CDN URL validation (regex against allowed domains) prevents SSRF and content injection while keeping the submission API lightweight.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: Cannot guarantee image availability at review time if the creator deletes the original post. Mitigated by URL reachability check during auto-validation.

technical_decisions.decision: Use database advisory lock on application_id to prevent concurrent submissions
alternatives_considered: Application-level mutex via Redis distributed lock
PostgreSQL advisory lock on application_id hash
technical_decisions.chosen: PostgreSQL advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock) on application_id hash
technical_decisions.rationale: Advisory lock is session-scoped, automatically released on transaction end, and does not require additional infrastructure (Redis). It prevents two concurrent submit requests from creating duplicate versions. Optimistic locking would allow the race to happen and then fail one request, which is acceptable but provides a worse UX.
technical_decisions.trade_offs: PostgreSQL-specific. If migrating to another database, would need to switch to Redis-based locking. Acceptable trade-off for v1.

submission_flow.description: End-to-end flow for a creator submitting content for a campaign

steps.action: Acquire advisory lock on application_id to prevent concurrent submissions
Validate preconditions: application exists and is accepted, content_deadline not passed, max revisions not exceeded, no version currently in auto_checking
Create ContentVersion row (version_number = current_version + 1), update ContentSubmission.current_version and status=auto_checking
Run validation pipeline synchronously: text_length_check → image_count_check → sensitive_word_check → image_quality_check
Each check returns {check_name, passed, detail}. Results are collected into a validation_result JSON array.
Save validation_result to ContentVersion. If all checks passed → status=pending_review. If any failed → status=auto_rejected.
Send notification: if pending_review → notify brand; if auto_rejected → notify creator with failure reasons
Release advisory lock (automatic on transaction commit). Return submission response with status and validation_result.

resubmission_flow.description: Flow for creator resubmitting revised content

steps.action: Creator calls POST /api/v1/submissions/{id}/resubmit with updated content
Validate: submission exists, user is the creator, status is auto_rejected or revision_requested, deadline not passed, revisions remaining > 0
Acquire advisory lock, create new ContentVersion with incremented version_number, then run the same validation pipeline as initial submission (steps 4-9 of submission_flow)
